```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

When your R code calls a hosted language model, the work happens in the
provider's datacenter. CodeCarbon measures the electricity *your machine*
draws, so it cannot see it. A **remote tracker** estimates that provider-side
impact instead, and it plugs into the same functions you already use:
`carbon_track()`, `carbon_track_all()`, `carbon_run()`, `carbon_step()` and
`tracker_start()` / `tracker_stop()`. The functions stay the same; only the
target changes.

This guide classifies the sentiment of eight product reviews with
`openai/gpt-6-luna` and tracks what the requests cost. The output shown is
from a real run.

## Setup

You need [ellmer](https://ellmer.tidyverse.org) and an API key. This guide
reaches the model through OpenRouter, so put the key in `~/.Renviron`:

```
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-...
```

With an OpenAI key, use `chat_openai(model = "gpt-6-luna")` instead;
everything else is identical.

```{r}
library(tidycarbon)
library(ellmer)
library(dplyr)
```

## The task

```{r}
reviews <- c(
  "Absolutely love this kettle, boils in under a minute.",
  "Stopped working after two weeks. Very disappointed.",
  "It does what it says. Nothing more, nothing less.",
  "The battery life is incredible, I charge it once a week.",
  "Customer service never replied to my emails.",
  "Arrived on time and matches the description.",
  "Far too loud for a bedroom fan, I sent it back.",
  "Best purchase I have made all year!"
)

chat <- chat_openrouter(
  model = "openai/gpt-6-luna",
  system_prompt = "You classify the sentiment of product reviews.",
  echo = "none"
)

sentiment_type <- type_array(items = type_object(
  id        = type_integer("Number of the review"),
  sentiment = type_enum(values = c("positive", "neutral", "negative"))
))

classify <- function(texts) {
  prompt <- paste0(seq_along(texts), ". ", texts, collapse = "\n")
  chat$chat_structured(prompt, type = sentiment_type)
}
```

All eight reviews go in one request and come back as a data frame.

## Create a remote tracker

Where `carbon_init()` creates a CodeCarbon tracker for your machine,
`carbon_init_remote()` creates a tracker for the provider. Give it the chat
your code uses:

```{r}
tracker <- carbon_init_remote(chat, project_name = "sentiment")
```

The `engine` argument selects the estimation method. It defaults to
`"ecologits"` ([EcoLogits](https://ecologits.ai)), currently the only one,
which is installed automatically through reticulate.

## Track the classification

```{r}
res <- carbon_track(classify, texts = reviews, tracker = tracker)

res$result[[1]]
#>   id sentiment
#> 1  1  positive
#> 2  2  negative
#> 3  3   neutral
#> 4  4  positive
#> 5  5  negative
#> 6  6   neutral
#> 7  7  negative
#> 8  8  positive
```

`res` is one tidy row: the result, plus the estimate for the requests made
while `classify()` ran.

```{r}
res |>
  select(duration, n_calls, n_modelled, output_tokens, engine, engine_version)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   duration n_calls n_modelled output_tokens engine    engine_version
#>      <dbl>   <int>      <int>         <dbl> <chr>     <chr>
#> 1     4.89       1          1           141 ecologits 0.11.2
```

The impact columns use CodeCarbon's names and units (`energy_consumed` in
kWh, `emissions_total` in kgCO2eq, `water_consumed` in L), each as a lower
and an upper bound:

```{r}
res |>
  transmute(
    energy_wh_min = energy_consumed_min * 1000,
    energy_wh_max = energy_consumed_max * 1000,
    co2e_mg_min   = emissions_total_min * 1e6,
    co2e_mg_max   = emissions_total_max * 1e6,
    water_ml_min  = water_consumed_min * 1000,
    water_ml_max  = water_consumed_max * 1000
  )
#> # A tibble: 1 × 6
#>   energy_wh_min energy_wh_max co2e_mg_min co2e_mg_max water_ml_min water_ml_max
#>           <dbl>         <dbl>       <dbl>       <dbl>        <dbl>        <dbl>
#> 1        0.0211        0.0225        9.48        10.0       0.0760       0.0810
```

It is a range because OpenAI does not publish the size of its models, so
EcoLogits brackets it.

## Look at the individual requests

The `calls` list-column holds one row per request, including how the model
name was matched to one EcoLogits knows:

```{r}
res$calls[[1]] |>
  select(provider, model, resolved_model, resolution,
         input_tokens, output_tokens, latency_s, grid_zone)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 8
#>   provider model     resolved_model resolution input_tokens output_tokens latency_s grid_zone
#>   <chr>    <chr>     <chr>          <chr>             <dbl>         <dbl>     <dbl> <chr>
#> 1 openai   openai/g… gpt-6-luna     exact               193           141      4.89 USA
```

Always check `resolution`. `"exact"` means the model is in the EcoLogits
registry. A model it does not know is either computed as the nearest model of
the same family (`"proxy: ..."`) or left out (`modelled = FALSE`, impacts
`NA`), and `n_modelled` in the summary row tells you how many requests were
actually estimated.

## Compare two prompting strategies

Does asking the model to justify each label cost more? Track both versions
with `carbon_track_all()`. Each version gets its own chat, and one tracker
watches both:

```{r}
chat_reason <- chat_openrouter(
  model = "openai/gpt-6-luna",
  system_prompt = "You classify the sentiment of product reviews.",
  echo = "none"
)

reason_type <- type_array(items = type_object(
  id        = type_integer("Number of the review"),
  sentiment = type_enum(values = c("positive", "neutral", "negative")),
  reason    = type_string("One sentence explaining the label")
))

classify_reason <- function(texts) {
  prompt <- paste0(seq_along(texts), ". ", texts, collapse = "\n")
  chat_reason$chat_structured(prompt, type = reason_type)
}

tracker <- carbon_init_remote(list(chat, chat_reason), project_name = "sentiment")

runs <- carbon_track_all(
  list(
    list(fun = classify,        args = list(texts = reviews)),
    list(fun = classify_reason, args = list(texts = reviews))
  ),
  tracker
)

runs |>
  mutate(strategy = c("label only", "label + reason")) |>
  transmute(strategy, n_calls, output_tokens,
            energy_wh_min = energy_consumed_min * 1000,
            energy_wh_max = energy_consumed_max * 1000)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 5
#>   strategy       n_calls output_tokens energy_wh_min energy_wh_max
#>   <chr>            <int>         <dbl>         <dbl>         <dbl>
#> 1 label only           1           141        0.0211        0.0225
#> 2 label + reason       1           269        0.0331        0.0357
```

The explanations nearly double the output tokens, and the estimate rises by
about 60%. Output length is what drives the estimate, so trimming what you
ask the model to write is the most direct way to lower it.

## Measure your machine and the provider together

The two trackers answer different questions, so each returns its own table.
To cover the same code with both, open one globally and pass the other:

```{r}
local <- carbon_init(project_name = "sentiment", measure_power_secs = 1)

tracker_start(local)
tracker_start(tracker)
res_local  <- carbon_track(classify, texts = reviews, tracker = local)
res_remote <- tracker_stop(tracker)
tracker_stop(local)

res_local |> select(duration, energy_consumed, emissions_total)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   duration energy_consumed emissions_total
#>      <dbl>           <dbl>           <dbl>
#> 1     4.41        0.000111       0.0000422

res_remote |> select(n_calls, energy_consumed_min, energy_consumed_max)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 3
#>   n_calls energy_consumed_min energy_consumed_max
#>     <int>               <dbl>               <dbl>
#> 1       1           0.0000218           0.0000233
```

Do not add the two. One is your machine, measured; the other is the
provider's datacenter, modelled.

## How to read the numbers

- **They are estimates, not measurements.** EcoLogits models inference from
  the model's size and the length of its output. Nothing is measured at the
  provider.
- **Only output tokens count.** The 193 input tokens above add nothing to the
  estimate, so a long prompt looks free. The upper bound is the upper bound
  for generating the output, not for the whole request.
- **The tracker sees the chats you gave it.** A chat that is cloned or
  created inside the tracked code is not seen, and its requests are not
  counted. `n_calls` tells you how many were.
- **Routing is invisible.** A request sent through OpenRouter is estimated
  as if the model's own provider served it from its usual datacenter.

## Where next

- `carbon_run()` and `carbon_step()` accept the same tracker for expressions
  and pipelines; collect a pipeline's log with `carbon_collect()`.
- For clients other than ellmer, build the requests table yourself with
  `carbon_calls()` and estimate it with `carbon_provider()`.
- To estimate a Claude Code session, see `calls_from_transcript()`.
